authority_note: The fix commit 13082834 was authored directly by the maintainer and is a superset of a parallel local attempt (it also removes the stale opcode-15 HeapFree arm and adds MVIR wire unit tests). The duplicate local commits were discarded in favour of this commit.

first_mismatch.detail: the writer emits `HeapFree` as opcode 17 with a single operand; the reader's opcode-17 arm decoded `Eq` with two operands (a stray duplicate of opcode 8). The reader's `HeapFree` lived at opcode 15, which the writer never emits.
first_mismatch.effect: each `HeapFree` was misread as `Eq`, consuming one extra operand (4+ bytes); the reader drifted and read a garbage block_count (83886080) -> allocation abort / `CorruptedData`

why_only_async: only async-lowered bodies emit `HeapFree` (the A2 future-environment free). Sync functions and generic async functions (whose bodies are not materialized) never emit it, so they round-tripped fine — which is why the A2-FU2 workaround (generic async) accidentally avoided the bug.

control_matrix.async_generic_one: PASSED before (body not materialized, no HeapFree)

fix: reader opcode 17 decodes `MlibInstruction::HeapFree { value }`; the stale opcode-15 HeapFree arm was removed
non_fixes_avoided: no special-case zero-parameter async on import
no re-mapping of CorruptedData to another diagnostic
bump: none — the serialized schema and the writer's emitted bytes are unchanged; only the decoder's wrong opcode arm was corrected, so previously-broken artifacts become readable rather than invalidated
verdict: FIND-ASYNC-PROVIDER-01: CLOSED / FIXED IN TESTED SCOPE at 13082834 (exported async providers survive the .llib boundary; nonzero-param, void, generic and sync controls all hold)
